Sucrose at higher concentrations provides conformational stability, and polysorbate80 offers interface protection. The best candidates will combine these elements while avoiding non-beneficial excipients like arginine or histidine.

EDTA is consistently present in the top formulations, indicating its importance in chelating metal ions that catalyse oxidative reactions. Sucrose at higher concentrations (around 70 mM) also appears to be beneficial for stability. Polysorbate80 seems to provide better interface protection compared to other surfactants when used with methionine and EDTA.
